memories.author: D05
memories.text: NAFLD diagnosed based on elevated liver enzymes and hepatic steatosis on ultrasound. Patient asymptomatic, BMI 22, non‑alcoholic, no significant alcohol intake. Examination: mild right upper quadrant tenderness, otherwise normal. LFT shows ALT 68 U/L, AST 45 U/L, platelets 210×10⁹/L. Lipid profile: LDL 130 mg/dL, triglycerides 180 mg/dL.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Silymarin 140 mg tablet, take one tablet three times daily. Rosuvastatin 5 mg tablet, take one tablet once daily at bedtime.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: ALT 68 U/L (7‑35), AST 45 U/L (8‑40), ALP 78 U/L (40‑129), GGT 32 U/L (0‑51). Total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (0.2‑1.2). Platelets 210×10⁹/L (150‑400). Lipids: Cholesterol 190 mg/dL (<200), HDL 42 mg/dL (>40), LDL 130 mg/dL (<100), Triglycerides 180 mg/dL (<150).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Abdominal ultrasound: liver size 14.5 cm, diffuse increased echogenicity consistent with steatosis. No focal lesion, spleen normal, portal vein patent. No ascites.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Follow‑up NAFLD. Patient reports occasional fatigue, no abdominal pain. Continues silymarin and rosuvastatin. Examination: BMI 22, liver edge not palpable, no jaundice. LFT shows ALT 55 U/L, AST 38 U/L. Lipids improved.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: ALT 55 U/L (7‑35), AST 38 U/L (8‑40), ALP 80 U/L (40‑129), GGT 30 U/L (0‑51). Platelets 208×10⁹/L. Lipids: Cholesterol 178 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, LDL 110 mg/dL, Triglycerides 140 mg/dL.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Rosuvastatin dose increased to 10 mg tablet once daily at bedtime. Silymarin unchanged 140 mg TDS.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: NAFLD review. Patient feels well, no new symptoms. Medication adherence good. Examination: BMI 22, no hepatomegaly. LFT: ALT 48 U/L, AST 34 U/L. Lipids within target.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: ALT 48 U/L (7‑35), AST 34 U/L (8‑40), ALP 77 U/L (40‑129), GGT 28 U/L (0‑51). Platelets 212×10⁹/L. Lipids: Cholesterol 170 mg/dL, HDL 45 mg/dL, LDL 95 mg/dL, Triglycerides 125 mg/dL.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2026-01-08 at 09:30 with Dr Suresh Menon for NAFLD follow‑up.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: NAFLD follow‑up. Patient mentions mild early‑morning fatigue, otherwise well. Continues silymarin and rosuvastatin 10 mg. Examination: BMI 22, liver not palpable, no jaundice. LFT shows ALT 52 U/L, AST 36 U/L.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been feeling a bit tired in the mornings for the past week, but it improves after breakfast. No other complaints.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: ALT 52 U/L (7‑35), AST 36 U/L (8‑40), ALP 79 U/L (40‑129), GGT 31 U/L (0‑51). Platelets 210×10⁹/L. Lipids: Cholesterol 172 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, LDL 100 mg/dL, Triglycerides 130 mg/dL.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Continue silymarin 140 mg TDS. Continue rosuvastatin 10 mg OD at bedtime.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: NAFLD review. Patient reports fatigue resolved, feels energetic. Medication adherence excellent. Examination: BMI 22, no hepatomegaly. LFT: ALT 38 U/L, AST 28 U/L. Lipids optimal.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: ALT 38 U/L (7‑35), AST 28 U/L (8‑40), ALP 75 U/L (40‑129), GGT 26 U/L (0‑51). Platelets 215×10⁹/L. Lipids: Cholesterol 165 mg/dL, HDL 46 mg/dL, LDL 88 mg/dL, Triglycerides 110 mg/dL.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Continue silymarin 140 mg TDS. Continue rosuvastatin 10 mg OD at bedtime.
